title: Recommendation snapshots, revert wizard, and cost inspector UX for Optimize console
creator: Arianna Chen
description: Build a consolidated UX for Optimize recommendation cards that includes immutable recommendation snapshots, a guided revert wizard, and an interactive cost inspector. The goal is to let customers preview batching and caching changes, simulate unit-cost and latency impact, safely apply configurations with checkpointed snapshots, and have a searchable, exportable apply history for auditing and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation card shows a read-only snapshot of the exact config proposal (batch size, kv cache rules, quantization profile) and expected unit savings with percentile ranges
Diff preview displays before/after config keyed to model, route, and sequence length distribution with an explainable list of optimizations applied
Apply flow creates an immutable snapshot and optional canary plan; UI surfaces checkpoint ID and links it to the apply history
Revert wizard walks users through selecting a snapshot, shows affected routes/models, estimates cost/latency impact of reverting, and creates a revert snapshot on completion
Cost inspector simulates traffic slices (50th/95th percentile) and shows estimated per-token cost and latency for both current and proposed configs
Audit trail stores: who applied, snapshot ID, exact diff, rollout plan, canary results, and revert actions; trail is searchable by snapshot ID, user, route, model
Exportable CSV/JSON of apply history for compliance exports and SOC/pen tests
RBAC gating: only users with Optimize.Apply role see the final "Apply" CTA; Approvers can be added to the apply modal
E2E tests for snapshot creation, apply, revert, and audit export exist in the test harness and are green on the acceptance pipeline
comments: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: PM + Design + Eng alignment meeting. Agreed to treat snapshots as immutable artifacts stored in Optimize backend. Decision: snapshots include metadata + full diff + simulated cost metrics.
2026-02-26 - Design critique: Jules Ortega suggested emphasizing affected routes/models in the card header to reduce cognitive load. Action: show compact model/route chips + breadcrumb.

2026-03-01 - Engineering review: ENG lead flagged storage size for snapshots if we store full model config for each recommendation. Trade-off: store diffs + compressed canonical configs. Engineering to prototype compression ratio and retention policy.

2026-03-04 - PM note: Add a revert preview that computes delta impact for a selected traffic slice. Samir will wire an initial RPC to runtime simulator (ENG-2481) for 95th percentile latency estimates.

2026-03-07 - Design -> Iteration 2: Figma prototype v2 uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/Optimize-Recommendation-Snapshots/v2 (internal). UI shows snapshot tag, author, timestamp, simulation graphs, and revert CTA.

2026-03-09 - Legal/Security flagged that apply history must be immutable for audit. Security suggested using append-only ledger in the backend. Security review required: true. Action: follow up with Security to define retention SLA.

2026-03-11 - PM sync: Implementing canary rollout options: percent-based or route-based. Will surface automatic fallback if latency degradation > threshold. Need to define default thresholds (proposal: +20% latency or +10% error rate).

2026-03-12 - Current: engineering spike complete. Prototype API endpoints: POST /optimize/snapshots, POST /optimize/applies, POST /optimize/reverts. Next step: integrate with Console components and add unit tests for RBAC gating. Links: PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/482
notes: Retention policy proposal: 90 days full snapshot retention for active customers, 365 days archive mode for enterprise (costed as add-on).
Consider adding a "simulate-only" role for non-prod users so SREs can run what-if scenarios without creating snapshots visible to billing teams.
Edge case: partial applies across multiple routes needs atomic snapshot behavior; implementation will use a transaction in the backend and a composed revert snapshot on rollback.
